title: U2’s First Album in Nine Years, ‘Carnaval De Luz,’ Will Feature a Dolly Parton Duet With Bono, Said to Be Her Last Recorded Vocal
description: For anyone waiting for years to get a U2 album again, it might have seemed as if the band was, you know, running to stand still. But the day is at h
body:
For anyone waiting for years to get a U2 album again, it might have seemed as if the band was, you know, running to stand still. But the day is at hand, as the group’s first full-length recording in nine years, “Carnaval De Luz,” has been set for a Nov. 12 release, Interscope Records announced Thursday.

	The concluding track on the album is a duet with Dolly Parton, “Torn,” described in a release as “what has sadly turned out to be her last recorded vocal performance.” The song was co-written by U2, Parton and Johnny McDaid, and is described as “a tender country song detailing broken family ties that holds wider resonances.” The track features pedal steel guitar from Daniel Lanois.
	

	The forthcoming album is being previewed with a new single, “Silencio,” released to DSPs in conjunction with the morning announcement. The song was described in a release as a “2mins 35second homage to early surf-punk insolence.”




	The 12 songs on the new album were characterized as “a collection of 12 songs exploring themes of spirituality, friendship, freedom and endurance in the face of dark, encroaching forces.” The set was produced by longtime collaborator Jacknife Lee.

	Other collaborators include Brian Eno (doing co-writing and synthesizer duty on “Go (Carnaval De Luz),” “The Greatest Show on Earth” and “Can’t Stop Us Now”), Martin Garrix (co-writing on “Glorify”), and Lanois (pedal steel on “Torn”), with additional production from Ryan Tedder on “Silencio.”
	

	Said Bono in a statement, “Roll up, roll up, roll up! Bring your purple socks, your broken hearts, your rose-tinted naivety… oh be amazed in the hall of mirrors. There will be loud guitars, deep bass, some ecstatic rhythms and, yes, some silver tears will make an appearance!

	“‘Cause in the near distance just outside our carnival of light there are all kinds of creatures… the same imagination that brings us our creativity can also bring us monsters. So we make the drums louder. We build a bigger fire. We make our stories wilder and funnier. We make the melodies sweeter and the songs, they better shine, because if the world is in darkness we better not be.”

	The band has been far from dormant lately, even if this is officially the first new album in nearly a decade. It was preceded by two surprise-release/digital-only EPs, “Days of Ash” and “Easter Lily,” each of them including six songs, released for Ash Wednesday and Easter, respectively. There is no overlap between those two EPs and the content of the new album, so U2 will have released 24 songs in a calendar year by the time “Carnaval De Luz” comes out — a productive way to celebrate the band’s 50th anniversary.

schema.headline: U2’s First Album in Nine Years, ‘Carnaval De Luz,’ Will Feature a Dolly Parton Duet With Bono, Said to Be Her Last Recorded Vocal

title: ‘Black Doves’ Season 2 Trailer: Keira Knightley Investigates Spy Murders With a New Team in Netflix Action Thriller
description:
Keira Knightley is back in the first trailer for Netflix’s “Black Doves” Season 2. All six hour-long episode will release on November 5.

	The logli
body:
Keira Knightley is back in the first trailer for Netflix’s “Black Doves” Season 2. All six hour-long episode will release on November 5.

	The logline for Season 2 teases: “Helen (Knightley) is still betraying her nation’s secrets to the covert organization she serves: the Black Doves. But after the misadventures of last Christmas, and with her husband Wallace (Andrew Buchan), preparing to become Prime Minister, she is walking a more treacherous line than ever. As Helen’s enigmatic handler Mrs. Reed (Sarah Lancashire) is ensnared in a ruthless plot to undermine her position in the Black Doves, Helen is reunited with her best friend Sam (Ben Whishaw). The once high-end triggerman is now reduced to lonely drinks in Soho bars and low-rate hits. As they search for answers, loyalties are weaponized, trust is shattered, and the fight to protect the people they love could cost everything. With all the explosive wit of Series 1, Helen and Sam’s mission leads them back to old friends and enemies, through the dark decisions and painful sacrifices of their pasts, and right to the heart of the Black Doves.”
	

	The Season 2 cast includes Knightley, Ben Whishaw, Sarah Lancashire, Andrew Buchan, Kathryn Hunter, Ella Lily Hyland, Gabrielle Creevy, Agnes O’Casey, Ambika Mod, Babou Ceesay, Sam Riley, Neve Campbell, Sylvia Hoeks, Goran Kostic and Samuel Barnett.


	The show is created and written by Joe Barton, who also executive produces. Knightley exeuctive produces alongside Jane Featherstone for Sister and Chris Fry. Julian Farino and Kieron Hawkes direct this season and Callum Devrell-Cameron produces.
	

	Watch the trailer below.

title: Netflix’s Animated Drama ‘In Waves’ Opens the American French Film Festival, TV Competition Set
description: Animated feature “In Waves,” directed by Phuong Mai Nguyen, opens the American French Film Festival Nov. 3 as the fest celebrates its 30th anniversa
body:
Animated feature “In Waves,” directed by Phuong Mai Nguyen, opens the American French Film Festival Nov. 3 as the fest celebrates its 30th anniversary.“In Waves” made its debut at the Cannes Film Festival earlier this year, where it was the first animated feature to kick off Critics’ Week. Adapted from AJ Dungo’s graphic novel, the feature is a love story between a shy teenage boy and the girl who teaches him how to surf and how to live, before she succumbs to cancer. The English-language voice cast includes Will Sharpe and Stephanie Hsu. The opening night screening is presented in association with Netflix.
	

	The festival runs Nov. 3-8 at the DGA complex in West Hollywood.


	“AJ Dungo, a Californian surfer and self-taught artist, spent years drawing his own graphic novel as a way of processing the loss of his girlfriend. That intimate, autobiographical work found its second life across the Atlantic, where French-Vietnamese director Phuong Mai Nguyen and Silex Films optioned it, assembled a French production and spent years translating Dungo’s linework into a fully animated feature. Netflix has now brought the finished film back to American audiences as the U.S. distributor, closing a circle that began on a California beach and passed through French animation studios before returning home. It is precisely this kind of journey — an American story reimagined through French artistry and craft, then returned to its origins — that sits at the heart of what TAFFF exists to celebrate,” says Cécile Rap-Veber, president of the Franco-American Cultural Fund (originator of TAFFF) and CEO of French org SACEM.
	

	The film has an organic tie to the festival. In 2024, TAFFF and the Writers Guild of America West presented the workshop “Bringing Graphic Worlds to Life,” in which Dungo and “In Waves” producer Priscilla Bertin explored the journey from page to screen.

	“I’m thrilled that ‘In Waves’ will open the American French Film Festival’s 30th anniversary edition — a first for an animated feature film,” said Ted Sarandos, co-CEO of Netflix. “As the ultimate stateside destination for French films and series, it’s an honor to have TAFFF’s support and I look forward to audiences around the world discovering this special film.”

	The festival’s lineup will be announced Oct. 6. But the festival also recognizes the artistry of the small screen. The 12 TV series competing for the TAFFF Audience Award and Jury Award have been announced, and they are:

	“Alice: Pioneer of Cinema,” directed by Virginie Verrier and Guillaume Lonergan and written by Tim Loane, Claire LeMaréchal and André Gulluni. The series stars Bérénice Bejo and explores the life of artist and entrepreneur Alice Guy.

	“All Shapes of Us,” created by Fanny Riedberger and directed by Jean-Baptiste Pouilloux and Elsa Bennett. Starring Catherine Frot, Claudia Tagbo, Ornella Fleury, Gérémy Crédeville and Marc Riso, the series follows the story of six teenagers as they navigate a new school year at the Hive, which specializes in eating disorders.

	“Laura’s Treatment,” created and written by Marie Kremer and Frédéric Krivine, and directed by Alim Iske). Series centers on Laura, a small-town pharmacist and mother who runs a support group for abuse victims. When authorities and the judicial system fail to protect the women and a group member is murdered, Laura takes matters into her own hands. Stars Valérie Bonneton.

	“Minimum Security,” created by John Wax and Gauthier Plancquaert. A comedy starring Audrey Lamy as the director of a French prison who mothers her blundering team of guards and inmates.

	“One Day We Will Make Love,” written and directed by Jérôme Bonnell. Natacha Krief and Édouard Sulpice star as two very different people with nothing in common except that they’ve both experienced a rough day, followed by a night together that was as joyful as it was boozy. But over the course of a weekend, love can blossom.
	

	“Paolo,” created by Sébastien Marnier. Jérôme Niel stars as Paolo, whose daily life is turned upside down when he reunites with Téophane (Yoann Gasiorowski), a former schoolmate who is now running for mayor of his city, and who, it seems, has everything going for him. What begins as simple admiration and a desire to support the campaign turns into a consuming obsession.

	“Prophet (A),” created by Abdel Raouf Dafri and Nicolas Peufaillit and based on Jacques Audiard’s feature “A Prophet.” Mamadou Sidibé stars as Malik, a young African immigrant, who must try to survive after being incarcerated for drug smuggling.

	“R 91,” created by Henri Debeurme and Mathilde Arnaud, and directed by Julien Despaux. The series, which stars Élodie Yung, Alban Lenoir, Patrick Mille and Jacques Gamblin, is set aboard the French nuclear-powered aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle during a strategic and highly volatile mission in the eastern Mediterranean. When a female crew member is found dead on board, and another goes missing shortly afterward, an investigator is rushed onto the ship to uncover what happened.

	“Rebounds: A History of Electro Dance,” written and directed by Loïc Phil and Marianne Getti. Doc series centers around Miel, dancer and choreographer Brandon Masele, as he explores the global evolution and history of electro dance and the Tecktonik phenomenon.

	“Singapura,” created and written by Elsa Marpeau; directed by Danielle Arbid. The crime thriller stars Nailia Harzoune as Justine, who arrives in Singapore, determined to reinvent herself and give her family a fresh start. In the tightly-knit world of French expatriates, she is captivated by Élisa (India Hair), an eccentric and tormented free spirit. But when a murder shakes their privileged circle, the buried secrets, lies, and betrayals begin to surface.

	“Someone Should Ban Sunday Afternoons,” created by Isabel Coixet. Starring Liv Henneguier, Clara Bretheau, Théo Christine, Balibar and Tim Robbins, the drama follows Louise, who has always dreamed of becoming a filmmaker, as she moves to Paris to be mentored by a legendary American writer-director. But reality quickly sets in and she discovers that Paris is tougher than she imagined.

	“Swapped,” written and created by Alexandra Echkenazi and Vincent Robert, and directed by Vania Leturcq and Savina Dellicour. Rose, played by Lula Cotton-Frapier, is a young woman who leaves her rural home in 19th-century Paris to work as a wet nurse for a wealthy, bourgeois family, only to find herself stepping into a dangerous and dark environment.
	

	The Television Series Competition is presented in association with Wild Bunch, Federation Studios, France TV Distribution, Disney+, Film & Picture, HBO Max, StudioCanal, SND Group M6 and Zorba Prods.

schema.headline: Netflix’s Animated Drama ‘In Waves’ Opens the American French Film Festival, TV Competition Set

title: Music Industry Moves: Chvrches Sign With Futures Music Group; MSG Entertainment Names Josephine Vaccarello President
description: Scottish pop trio Chvrches have signed with Futures Music Group and alongside that announcement have released their first single in three years, “Ro
body:
Scottish pop trio Chvrches have signed with Futures Music Group and alongside that announcement have released their first single in three years, “Roses.” The group will play two shows in the U.K. next month, in London and their hometown of Glasgow; the release follows singer Lauren Mayberry’s solo album on Island last year.

	Futures Music Group, founded by Derek Davies of Neon Gold and Dave Wallace of Avenue A, is an independent label collective separate from those companies with “transparent deal structures [and] integrated technology partnerships,” with deal structures designed to align incentives with artists, prioritizing long-term partnership and participation over traditional ownership models.” Founded in 2024, the collective’s roster includes Lykke Li, Mt. Joy, Cavetown, Phantogram, the Knocks and others.
	

	+ Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp. has named Josephine Vaccarello as its president. In this elevated role she will oversee the strategy and operations of multiple areas of the business, comprising all non-New York Knicks and New York Rangers sports bookings, as well as the productions business, which includes the Radio City Rockettes and the Christmas Spectacular Starring the Radio City Rockettes. In addition to her responsibilities at MSG Entertainment, she will continue to oversee booking live concert residencies and touring acts at Sphere, which is owned by Sphere Entertainment Co. and is part of the MSG Family of Companies. She was most recently the company’s EVP of live.


	“Over her nearly thirty-year career with MSG, Josephine has not only been instrumental in growing our live event business but also established herself as one of the industry’s most impactful and respected leaders,” said Jim Dolan, Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of MSG Entertainment and Sphere Entertainment. “Her deep understanding of our businesses and unparalleled industry relationships will continue to be an asset in this new role as we execute on our strategic vision for the Company, including identifying innovative growth opportunities and furthering our leadership position in live experiences.”
	

	+ Primary Wave Music has struck a partnership with the estate of the legendary R&B/pop singer Robert Palmer that reaches across his publishing and recording catalog, as well as share in his name, image, and likeness rights. The catalog includes such songs as the 1985 smash “Addicted to Love” as well as hits like “Bad Case Of Loving You (Doctor, Doctor),” “Simply Irresistible,” “Johnny & Mary,” “She Makes My Day,” and others, as well as collaborative hits such as “Some Like It Hot” with the Power Station and “I’ll Be Your Baby Tonight” with UB40. A soulful and versatile singer, Palmer had an unusually far-reaching career that also included collaborations with New Orleans legends the Meters. He passed away in 2003, shortly after the release of his final album, “Drive.”

	A rep for the estate said, “We are very excited to partner with Primary Wave. As we continue to honor Robert’s incredible legacy, we also look forward to working with the team on exploring ways to bring his music to both new and existing audiences, preserving his lasting impact for years to come.”

	Samantha Rhulen, Primary Wave’s SVP of Business & Legal Affairs, added, “Robert Palmer was a truly unique artist whose distinctive voice, songwriting, and style left an indelible mark on popular music. His catalog continues to resonate with audiences, and we are honored to welcome his incredible body of work to the Primary Wave family.

	+ U.K.-based garage artist-producer MPH has signed with DisOrder/Capitol Records, which will release his new album, “Here, Forever,” on November 20. He launches a U.S. tour on Oct. 2 in Portland, OR that continues through the end of November. He has collaborated with or remixed tracks by Calvin Harris, Chris Lake, Anderson .Paak, Four Tet, Sammy Virji, Tokimonsta and others.

	+ The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) has named Jackson Wagener Senior Vice President and Head of General Licensing, effective January 1, 2027. Reporting to ASCAP Executive Vice President and Head of Licensing Stephanie Ruyle, Wagener will oversee the team that licenses ASCAP’s repertory of over 20 million musical works to restaurants, bars, hotels, airlines, fitness studios, live music venues and other establishments. A 12-year veteran of ASCAP, Wagener currently serves as Senior Vice President, Business and Legal Affairs, a role he has held since 2020. He previously held roles at Greenberg Traurig and Weil, Gotshal & Manges.
	

	“Jackson pairs deep legal expertise with a clear sense of what licensees want and music creators need in today’s world,” said Ruyle. “In a rapidly changing market, he is uniquely equipped to pioneer the kind of innovative licensing solutions that make it easier than ever for businesses to utilize music, while ensuring songwriters are fairly compensated for performances of their work.”

	+ Chrysalis Records, part of the Reservoir group of companies, has announced a new integrated marketing structure for its London-based team. The team will continue to be led by Senior Vice President of Marketing James Meadows, with Colin Rice, Chrysalis Records Marketing Director overseeing the label’s roster and leading marketing campaigns.

	The label has also expanded Roman Tagoe’s responsibilities, under the new title of Digital Partnerships Director. Joining the digital team is Matt Sherratt, most recently with Amuse, in the newly created post of Head of Audience Development. The label also welcomes Jonny Halliday, who joins from Fire Records in the role of Marketing Manager. Alongside the new appointments, Grace Campbell has been appointed Associate Marketing Manager and Marianne Frederick has taken on the role of Senior Vice President, Production & Distribution. Eva Davies has been promoted into the newly created role of Project Coordinator, working closely with Frederick on frontline production.

	+ Entertainment attorney Sasha Safavi, most recently of UnitedMasters, has launched launch Syndicate, a law firm whose initial roster includes the sports media company Overtime, the streaming service Audiomack, Rebellion Records and a variety of artists and producers, as well as UnitedMasters. Safavi’s previous roles include stints at TuneCore and work with UnitedMasters’ sister company Translation.

schema.headline: Music Industry Moves: Chvrches Sign With Futures Music Group; MSG Entertainment Names Josephine Vaccarello President

title: Charlie Brooker’s New Netflix Series Gets Title, ‘Blackmere,’ as Rory Kinnear Joins Cast and First-Look Photos Revealed
description: Charlie Brooker‘s new Netflix series has revealed its title — “Blackmere” — not to be confused with the writer and producer’s other show for the str
body:
Charlie Brooker‘s new Netflix series has revealed its title — “Blackmere” — not to be confused with the writer and producer’s other show for the streamer, “Black Mirror.” 

	Netflix announced the show’s title, some first-look images and the news that Rory Kinnear (“The Diplomat,” “Black Mirror”) has joined the cast at its U.K. upfronts in London on Thursday. Kinnear stars alongside Paddy Considine, Georgina Campbell and Lena Headey in the four-part series, coming early 2027, which is described as an “absurd comedy disguised as an incredibly serious crime thriller,” according to its synopsis. 
	

	“Tormented Detective John Blackmere (Considine) leaves the rain-soaked Northern city of Bleakford for London to avenge his partner’s death and catch a ritualistic serial killer before they run out of victims,” the plot description continues. “Contains blood and frowning.”


	“Blackmere” was created and written by Brooker, with co-writers including Ben Caudell, Jason Hazeley, Emer Kenny, Daniel Maier and Joel Morris, plus additional material by Victoria Asare Archer. Brooker executive produces alongside Jessica Rhoades and Annabel Jones, with Mark Kinsella co-executive producing and Richard Webb producing. Al Campbell is the series director. 

	Brooker’s new series was first announced last year as the “Untitled Charlie Brooker Project.” “I’m beyond thrilled to be saying these words for the press release. I’ve dreamt of providing a quote ever since I was a young foetus, and now here I am doing it,” Brooker said at the time. “I’d pinch myself, but like all of us, I’m terrified that if I do that, I might wake up and discover 2025 has all been a magical dream. Please watch my show. I am begging you.”
	

	Besides “Blackmere,” Brooker’s highly successful “Black Mirror” is set to return to Netflix for an eighth season, which started production this summer. 

	See more first-look photos below.

title: ‘Day Drinker’ Trailer: Johnny Depp’s Hollywood Comeback Continues in a Twisty Thriller With Penélope Cruz and Madelyn Cline
description: Lionsgate has released a trailer for “Day Drinker,” the Marc Webb-directed thriller starring Johnny Depp, Madelyn Cline and Penélope Cruz. The film
body:
Lionsgate has released a trailer for “Day Drinker,” the Marc Webb-directed thriller starring Johnny Depp, Madelyn Cline and Penélope Cruz. The film will hit theaters on March 26, 2027.

	“Day Drinker” follows a private-yacht bartender (Cline) as she encounters a mysterious guest (Depp in extra-weird mode). The official logline adds: “They soon find themselves entangled with a criminal figure (Cruz) and connected in ways no one saw coming.”
	

	In the eerie trailer, audiences get a glimpse of a grey-haired Depp, who says, ominously: “My story? Perhaps it’s a tale of revenge. Or perhaps something worse. What if all of this is a ghost story? Or maybe I’m just another day drinker?”


	The film will be one of the first Hollywood-supported movies to bring Depp back to the big screen after his 2022 trial against ex-wife Amber Heard; his other film, Paramount’s “Ebenezer,” will be in theaters on Nov. 13. “Day Drinker” also brings Cruz back to the Hollywood studio system after dominating 2026 with a slew if well-reviewed indie productions, including “La Bola Negra,” “The Invite” and “Bunker.”

	“Day Drinker” is Cline’s first project since wrapping “Outer Banks,” the North Carolina-set Netflix show that made her a star as series regular Sarah Cameron. Season 1 premiered in 2020, and the show concluded with Season 5 in August.

	“Day Drinker” is produced by Basil Iwanyk, Erica Lee, Adam Kolbrenner, Zach Dean and Nathan Kahane, and is executive produced by Webb, Dan Friedkin, Micah Green, Daniel Steinman, Stephen Deuters, Jason Forman, Sam Sarkar, Eric Sherman, Sarah Hong, Scott LaStaiti, Adrián Guerra and Xavier Parache
	

	Watch the trailer below.

schema.headline: ‘Day Drinker’ Trailer: Johnny Depp’s Hollywood Comeback Continues in a Twisty Thriller With Penélope Cruz and Madelyn Cline

title: Ex-Disney CEO Bob Chapek Says Bob Iger Ran ‘Relentless Three-Year Campaign’ to Fire Him: ‘Made It Seem as If I Had Committed Some Terrible Offense’
description: Former Disney CEO Bob Chapek claims his predecessor-turned-successor Bob Iger underwent a “relentless three-year campaign to push me out” after init
body:
Former Disney CEO Bob Chapek claims his predecessor-turned-successor Bob Iger underwent a “relentless three-year campaign to push me out” after initially appointing him to the job.

	“The way Disney’s board and Bob Iger handled my firing made it seem as if I had committed some terrible offense,” Chapek writes in an excerpt from his upcoming book “Behind the Castle Walls,” which was published by Vanity Fair Thursday. “To outsiders, it looked suspicious—who gets ousted on a Sunday, right before a company’s big event, unless they’re guilty of something?”
	

	Chapek took over the Disney CEO job in February 2020 — as Iger’s hand-picked successor. But in November 2022, the Disney board ousted Chapek after a series of missteps and called Iger back into service. (Iger stepped down as CEO this March, replaced by former parks head Josh D’Amaro.)


	“From the moment he announced my appointment, he clearly regretted it and seemed to initiate a relentless three-year campaign to push me out,” Chapek writes of Iger. “From day one as CEO, I had respected the board’s decision to have him remain as executive chairman, directing creative endeavors and overseeing the transition until late 2021. I’d always made it clear I had big shoes to fill. But I’d never expected to endure a drawn-out, purposeful undoing of my leadership.”

	Disney declined to comment Thursday. Iger declined to comment via a representative at Thrive Capital, where Iger is now a partner.

	Disney insiders are said to view Chapek’s book as a “revisionist” account of the events that transpired. 
	

	Published by Simon & Schuster, “Behind the Castle Walls” is set to release Sept. 29. While Chapek is making the rounds promoting the book with today’s Vanity Fair excerpt and an interview published by the Wall Street Journal Wednesday, according to industry sources, the title remains in stiff competition with Wall Street Journal reporter Robbie Whelan’s upcoming unauthorized “The House of Mouse: Bob Iger and The War of Succession at Disney,” which is slated for release on Dec. 1, 2026.

	In the new book excerpt, Chapek goes on to recall a story from Iger’s retirement party in which Chapek claims he was the butt of a “snide” joke about his upbringing in Indiana and then overlooked when it came time for Iger to conclude his speech by passing the torch.

	“He continued, going through the next few phases of his career, but still had yet to mention anything about his eventual replacement,” Chapek wrote. “It was a retirement party after all. Eventually, he got to the end, and I braced myself for what was next. ‘And as I come to this point in my career where I’m ready now to, you know, move on to my next chapter . . .’ he said as his voice trailed off. He stopped again, turned, and then abruptly declared, ‘You know what? I think I’ve said enough. Thank you very much. Good night.’ I mean, literally, there wasn’t a head that didn’t turn around and look at me like, Oh my God, he just literally blew you off. That moment encapsulates how Iger treated our professional transition. He could have said, I turn the reins over to my successor, and I wish him all the luck in the world. That’s all he had to say. It didn’t need to be an endorsement. It just didn’t need to be venomous. He couldn’t even stay neutral. That proved too much for him. He had to disrespect me and my background.”

	Chapek also claims that while he worked to “ensure the company survived the COVID shutdown under the crushing debt of a newly minted and exorbitant Fox deal,” Iger “seemed to spend his time finding ways to politically outmaneuver and undermine me.” The ousted Disney CEO calls out the backlash over Disney’s position regarding the “Don’t Say Gay” bill as a particular instance in which he claims Iger tried to negatively impact Chapek’s image.

	“He interjected himself publicly in a way that would of course blow up on me, as I believe it was intended to, in the company’s response to the ‘Don’t Say Gay’ bill,” Chapek wrote. “While I was under pressure to keep the company afloat with no revenue and mounting debt, he appeared to actively work against me. As I pushed for bold streaming strategies to transform Disney into a streaming media powerhouse, he fueled an ego-driven power struggle.”

schema.headline: Ex-Disney CEO Bob Chapek Says Bob Iger Ran ‘Relentless Three-Year Campaign’ to Fire Him: ‘Made It Seem as If I Had Committed Some Terrible Offense’

title: ‘The Graham Norton Show,’ With Its Taylor Swift-Fueled Momentum, Lands Two-Year Pickup at BBC America and AMC Global Media Streamers (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Graham Norton’s couch is staying put on this side of the pond. As the U.K.-based host’s long-running talker “The Graham Norton Show” returns for its
body:
Graham Norton’s couch is staying put on this side of the pond. As the U.K.-based host’s long-running talker “The Graham Norton Show” returns for its Season 34 premiere next week, the show’s U.S. distribution has already been secured for two more seasons by AMC Global Media.

	That means “The Graham Norton Show” will remain on BBC America — its linear stateside home for many years — through Seasons 34 (2026-2027) and 35 (2027-2028), while also continuing on three AMC Global Media streaming platforms: Acorn TV, AMC+ and All Reality. Last season averaged 153,000 linear viewers on BBC America, its best performance in three years, while Acorn TV (where most of the streaming audience watches) saw a year-over-year bump and AMC+ more than doubled its streaming audience over the previous season.
	

	“He’s a singular talent,” said Courtney Thomasma, AMC Global’s exec VP of linear and streaming products. “He is just everything you want in a host. He’s warm and engaging and charismatic. He is an incredibly skilled interviewer, and I think he’s built a format that we call the ultimate late night celebrity dinner party … We talk about how his show really sits at the perfect intersection of a sort of uniquely British sophistication and broad pop culture appeal.”


	For Norton, who is signed in the U.K. with BBC One to continue his show through at least 2029, it’s an opportunity to continue expanding his audience in the U.S. as well.

	“We’ve had a loyal fan base in America for a long time,” Norton said. “It’s an odd thing. When I go to America, I don’t feel like anybody knows who I am. But there are certain situations where they do, and this must speak to the demographic of who watches this thing. If I go to a Broadway theater, everyone, all the kids who work there, know who I am. I can’t explain that, but it’s very nice. I often get a free drink!”
	



	

	



	Of course, Norton got plenty of global attention earlier this year when he appeared in Taylor Swift’s music video for “Opalite” — along with the guests she sat alongside on Norton’s couch in a Season 33 episode: Cillian Murphy, Domhnall Gleeson, Greta Lee, Jodie Smith and Lewis Capaldi.

	“The Swifties know the show because she’s been on multiple times, and wherever she appears, they will find her,” Norton said. “They’re not going to ignore a show that she’s on, so they all knew who I was, but there must have been people who encountered that video going, ‘Who are these people? Why is this very strange ragtag of people all together in a video?’ And of course, there were the conspiracy theories where they thought we had filmed the video before the show, and that’s why everyone was on the show with her, rather than the other way around.”

	In premiering the video, Swift called “The Graham Norton Show” one of her favorite programs, and even described Norton as “the insanely charismatic and lovable host” who “invites a random group of actors, entertainers, musicians, etc. to be on his show and we all sit there and chat like it’s a dinner party.” Not a bad promo from the global superstar.

	Norton credited that kind of positive on-set vibe, as described by Swift, for why the show has lasted for 34 seasons and counting. “We never imagined we would be this long-running, but we knew we wanted to keep going,” he said. “You can have those viral moments, and you can have those standout things and clips that get loads of attention. But if the people in the clips aren’t having a good time, they’re not going to come back. We need returning guests. Here in Britain, there have been talk shows in the past where they had gotcha moments or embarrassed the guests. That’s not sustainable.”

	Norton’s guest list from Season 33 proved that his philosophy is working: Besides Swift, it included Dwayne Johnson, Emily Blunt, Matthew McConaughey, Julia Roberts, Colin Farrell, Benedict Cumberbatch, Bruce Springsteen, Jeremy Allen White, Jennifer Lawrence, Tessa Thompson, Kim Kardashian, Glen Powell, Michelle Yeoh, Kate Hudson, Ben Stiller, Timothée Chalamet, Emma Thompson, Laura Dern, Cynthia Erivo, Halle Berry, Chris Hemsworth, Jacob Elordi, Jennifer Garner, Charli XCX and many more.
	

	“I really like interviews on podcasts, but we are a different beast in that I can’t imagine a podcast that would get the people we get all at the same time, all together on a couch,” Norton said. “The other thing I think that totally changes the conversation and the tenor of the interview is that we’re doing it in front of a big audience. I think people behave differently in front of an audience. They tell stories differently in front of an audience.”

	Norton said the show “takes a lot of moving parts and a lot of people and a lot of research,” and he admitted that with that much infrastructure, in this day and age, “maybe my show isn’t sustainable. Maybe this is the last throw of the dice.”

	At the same time, he knows the talk environment has become even tougher in the U.S., with shows like “The Late Show With Stephen Colbert,” “Conan” and “The Late Late Show With James Corden” already going away.

	“I imagine it is mostly financial,” he said. “In some way, I think Trump is keeping [the remaining] shows alive because they can’t cancel them. Otherwise, it looks like they’re caving to Trump.”

	But as a weekly program, “The Graham Norton Show” doesn’t carry the same kind of demands that the U.S. chat shows, most of which run four days a week, have. “I’m in the glorious position of putting a show out once a week,” Norton said. “Why would I quit? It’s the nicest job in show business!”

	Indeed, Norton added that with his BBC deal not up until 2029, he’s got time to figure out whether to continue. “I’m 65 at some point, and that sounds like a retirement age. But the world is changing, and it’s not like I’m big into gardening or beekeeping. I still really like my job, but equally I’m aware that I’m in an area of television where we are running out of road … It’s one thing to get a show on TV, but keeping it on TV for as long as we’ve been on is a larger slice of the pie than we deserve. So I’m really grateful.”

	Here in the U.S., AMC Global Media has found that “The Graham Norton Show” garners unique audiences depending on the platform. Besides its long run on BBC America, it also has a natural resonance with Acorn TV viewers who already have an affinity for British culture, Thomasma said. Then, in adding “Graham Norton” to the new, younger and more female-skewing All Reality platform, “we found that we’re now reaching a newer pop culture celebrity-driven audience that are discovering Graham for the first time,” she said. “It’s been a really interesting way of seeing the universal appeal of the genre, but potentially different entry points for different audiences. Our data has shown that most of the viewing across platforms is complementary via very minimal duplication in terms of the Graham audience.”
	

	Season 34 premieres in the U.K. on Friday, Sept. 25, and hits the U.S. platforms the following Thursday, Oct. 1. New episodes continue through March with that cadence — Thursdays here in the U.S. on BBC America and the AMC+, Acorn and All Reality streamers.

	Guests on the premiere episode include Tom Cruise (promoting his new film “Digger”), Florence Pugh (“East of Eden”), comedian/actor Lolly Adefoe (who’s taking on the lead role in “Oh, Mary!”) and comic John Bishop. Also, Emeli Sandé will perform.

	Norton said in interviewing Cruise, “I never get over the fact that it’s Tom Cruise. Mostly when you meet a big celebrity, after a while, it’s just a woman in a dress or a man in a suit, and you’re just talking to them. But he remains Tom Cruise throughout. I’ve met him socially at things, and to me, he’s always Tom Cruise. I don’t know what that’s about, and there aren’t many people who can do that. There is an electricity in the studio when he comes on.”

	Among Norton’s guests in Week 2 will be Catherine Zeta-Jones, whose U.K. thriller series “Kill Jackie” will run on AMC+ in the U.S. “That’s an opportunity where we’re able to mine and promote and educate our viewers about a favorite personality and then something that they can watch on our platforms,” Thomasma said.

schema.headline: ‘The Graham Norton Show,’ With Its Taylor Swift-Fueled Momentum, Lands Two-Year Pickup at BBC America and AMC Global Media Streamers (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Girl With the Dragon Tattoo’ Series at Sky to Star David Oyelowo and Viola Prettejohn
description:
Sky‘s “The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo” series has found its leads in David Oyelowo and Viola Prettejohn.

	Oyelowo (“Silo,” “Selma”) will play disg
body:
Sky‘s “The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo” series has found its leads in David Oyelowo and Viola Prettejohn.

	Oyelowo (“Silo,” “Selma”) will play disgraced journalist Mikael Blomkvist alongside Prettejohn (“The Crown,” “The Testament of Ann Lee”) as hacker Lisbeth Salander in a TV reimagining of Steig Larsson’s hit Millennium book series. The characters were portrayed by Daniel Craig and Rooney Mara, respectively, in David Fincher’s 2011 movie of the same name.
	

	Produced by Left Bank Pictures, known for “The Crown” and “Dept Q,” the eight-part mystery thriller promises to bring the story “into the present day” by “exploring how power, secrecy and misogyny take on new and insidious forms in an ever more connected digital world.” Oscar-nominated “King Richard” helmer Reinaldo Marcus Green has also come on board as lead director and an executive producer. Filming begins in Lithuania next month.


	“The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo” follows “canceled star journalist Mikael Blomkvist and uncompromising hacker Lisbeth Salander as they investigate the disappearance of Harriet Vanger, who vanished more than three decades ago from the secluded island home of one of Sweden’s most powerful industrial dynasties,” according to the show’s synopsis. “As they delve deeper into the Vanger family’s buried past, their investigation draws them closer to a chilling threat unfolding dangerously close to them in the present.”

	Variety broke the news that the series had been commissioned back in January. In addition to Green as director, “The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo” is written and executive produced by Amanda Coe (“Apple Tree Yard,” “The Trial of Christine Keeler”), Steve Lightfoot (“Behind Her Eyes,” “The Punisher”) and Angela LaManna (“The Haunting of Bly Manor,” “Behind Her Eyes”). Andrea Harkin (“The Trial of Christine Keeler,” “Time”) and Amy Neil (“Hanna,” “Hostage”) will also direct. Oyelowo is executive producing along with Charlotte Moore and John Phillips for Left Bank Pictures and Sam Hoyle for Sky, in addition to Scott Rudin and Amy Pascal. Nuala O’Leary is series producer. 
	

	“Lisbeth Salander and Mikael Blomkvist are two of modern fiction’s most iconic and compelling characters, and we’re thrilled to have Viola and David bringing them to life for a new generation,” Meghan Lyvers, managing director of scripted originals at Sky, said in a statement. “Our brilliant writing team, Reinaldo Marcus Green’s bold vision and our fantastic partners at Left Bank Pictures are creating a series that honors everything audiences love about ‘The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo,’ while taking its characters, mystery and themes into a world that feels unmistakably of the moment. We can’t wait for audiences to experience it.”

	Added Moore: “We are incredibly proud to have assembled a world class creative team to reimagine Stieg Larsson’s masterpiece for a modern audience. ‘The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo’ is an iconic story with themes of power, corruption, justice and violence against women that feel even more timely today. In Viola Prettejohn and David Oyelowo, we have two extraordinary actors at the heart of this adaptation and really look forward to audiences enjoying their take on these compelling and complex characters.”

	“The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo” will air on Sky in the U.K., Ireland, Italy, Germany, Switzerland and Austria. Sony Pictures Television is handling international distribution and will introduce global clients to the series at Mipcom in October.

	Deadline Hollywood was the first to report the news.

schema.headline: ‘Girl With the Dragon Tattoo’ Series at Sky to Star David Oyelowo and Viola Prettejohn

title: Macklemore Announces ‘Free Palestine’ Tour With All Ticket Sales Being Donated to Charity
description: Macklemore has announced the “Free Palestine” tour, with three shows set for Dublin (Oct. 26), Paris (Oct. 29) and London (Oct. 30). The news comes
body:
Macklemore has announced the “Free Palestine” tour, with three shows set for Dublin (Oct. 26), Paris (Oct. 29) and London (Oct. 30). The news comes after the Grammy-winning rapper was infamously dropped as opener from Ed Sheeran‘s U.S. tour after making “Free Palestine” speeches while on stage at two concerts at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

	Per Live Nation, the “Free Palestine” tour will “bring Macklemore together with artists and friends for a series of performances that center Palestine and Palestinians, and help provide humanitarian aid and support to the movement.”
	

	Additionally, all proceeds from the concerts will benefit the following organizations: Anera, Glia, Gaza Soup Kitchen, Taawon, HEAL Palestine, Palestinian Youth Movement, Middle East Children’s Alliance, Jewish Voice for Peace, Medical Aid for Palestinians. Institute for Middle East Understanding, Palestine Children’s Relief Fund and UNRWA USA.


	“If these last couple of weeks have shown us anything, it’s that something has shifted over the last three years,” Macklemore wrote in a statement on Instgaram while announcing the tour. “There has been a collective awakening around Palestinian liberation, the power of billionaires that try to censor that call, and what we expect from artists right now.”

	“It’s 2026. Being apolitical during a genocide doesn’t work anymore,” he continued. “People are asking artists to show up, educate themselves and be in community. To use the stage for more than entertainment. To push back when the call for a Free Palestine is met with attempts to silence it… What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage. When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention.”
	

	After Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran’s tour, he announced he was donating the entire $1 million salary he earned to organizations supporting Palestine. The rapper said he was dropped from Sheeran’s tour after Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft refused to let Macklemore play at the venue due to his vocal support for Palestine. Kraft allegedly was talking to other stadium owners to get them to ban Macklemore as well, forcing the tour promoters to drop the rapper.

	Kraft responded by claiming that both he and Sheeran would be donating $2 million each to “aid in the region to fight this humanitarian crisis,” although no specific organizations were listed. After Macklemore was dropped from the tour, Sheeran posted a statement that ignited widespread backlash against him as he explained why, unlike Macklemore, he does not speak out on political issues.

	“Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care. Nor does it mean I don’t support causes in my own, personal way,” the singer wrote. “There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds. Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace. I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change.”

	Sheeran changed his tune at his Sept. 19 concert, which marked his first show since Macklemore was dropped from the tour. The singer told the crowd after receiving backlash for staying silent that “this is a humanitarian issue, and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore.”

	“What happened in Israel and at the Nova Music Festival on Oct. 7 was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable, and disproportionate,” Sheeran said. “Our hearts can be broken by the scale of devastation and loss of civilians’ lives, children’s lives and the systemic injustice we’re seeing unfold in the West Bank cannot be overlooked.”
	

	Reach Macklemore’s full statement below.

title: President Trump Winces During U.S. Military Flyover With Xi Jinping: Video
description:
President Trump
                          Winces During ROARING Military Flyover
body:
President Trump
                          Winces During ROARING Military Flyover
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 24, 2026
                            5:59 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            President Trump rolled out the red carpet for Chinese leader Xi Jinping for his state visit to Washington D.C. — personally greeting Xi when he landed Wednesday night — but then things took a ROARING turn for the worse!
      
    
            That's right ... Trump got the shock of his life, it seems, while the two presidents were standing on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland as the U.S. military conducted a VERY LOUD flyover. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Check out the video ... Trump shoots a painful wince as U.S. Air Force jets roar overhead ... whereas Xi takes it all in stride, calmly looking up into the sky at the aircrafts with his wife, Peng Liyuan, by his side.  
      

            First Lady Melania Trump was also present for the flyover, but didn't seem too bothered by it as she stood behind the commander-in-chief. Melania and Donald warmly greeted Xi and his wife on the red carpet after China's power couple landed at the base with a lot of pomp and circumstance.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            You may recall ... Xi extended a similar welcome to Trump during his state visit to China in May, which also included a ceremonial carpet and soldiers standing at attention.
      
    
            Last night marked the first time in decades a U.S. president met a world leader at Joint Base Andrews. In 1962, President John F. Kennedy met British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan at the Air Force base.

title: 10-Year-Old Boy and Fifth Grade Teacher Found Dead During Iowa School Field Trip
description:
Deadly Iowa School Field Trip
                          10-Year-Old Boy And Teacher Found Dead In
body:
Deadly Iowa School Field Trip
                          10-Year-Old Boy And Teacher Found Dead In Reservoir
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 24, 2026
                            7:10 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A 10-year-old boy and his fifth-grade teacher were found dead Wednesday during a frantic police search after they went missing and ultimately drowned in an Iowa reservoir during a school field trip.
      
    
            The Johnson County Sheriff’s Office issued a statement Wednesday night, announcing that its deputies and other law enforcement agencies discovered the bodies of Ahmed Osman, 10, and Hannah Jorgensen, 24, floating in the water at the Coralville Reservoir in Iowa City.
      
    
            The Sheriff's Office called their deaths a "tragic accident" that occurred while the two were on a field trip with a bunch of fifth graders from Borlaug Elementary School at Lake MacBride State Park near the Coralville Reservoir.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Police are still piecing together how the pair wound up dead in the water. The Johnson County Medical Examiner will perform autopsies to determine their cause and manner of death.
      
    
            According to police ... Osman and Jorgensen vanished Tuesday, prompting a massive response from law enforcement agencies that fanned out looking for the duo until they were finally found at the reservoir the next afternoon.

body:
Minnesota Mayor
                          Sued Over MILF Remark, Penis Jokes
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 24, 2026
                            8:40 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The mayor of St. Paul, Minnesota, allegedly branded herself a "MILF," made cracks about the size of her police chief's penis, framed doctored pics emphasizing his bulge, and twice put her hand high on his thigh ... and now he's suing her for sexual harassment.
      
    
            Police Chief Axel Henry filed a lawsuit Wednesday against Mayor Kaohly Her and the city, accusing the mayor of sexual harassment, battery, and retaliation.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The "MILF" moment allegedly came at a February police academy graduation, when the mayor spotted an "MFF" ribbon on Henry's uniform -- short for Mobile Field Force.
      
    
            She allegedly said ... "Oh, I thought it said MILF so maybe I could get one" ... but Henry apparently wasn't amused, giving her a hard pass and walking away.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Henry says the raunchy behavior didn't stop there ... he alleges the mayor made sexual innuendos about his penis and photoshopped his face and those of other officers onto shirtless bodybuilders and UFC fighters with "prominent bulges" in their compression shorts.
      
    
            The mayor also allegedly printed the images, put them in gold frames, and placed them in Henry's office.
      
    
            Henry claims the mayor twice put her hand on his upper thigh beneath a conference-room table during a budget meeting -- allegedly moving closer to his groin the second time.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            He further accuses the mayor of calling officers "beefy," making orgasm-like noises while working out near cops and sending staff a "Weiner Wednesday" meme.
      
    
            Henry says the city retaliated after he complained by sidelining him from personnel decisions ... withholding records and publicly minimizing his allegations.
      
    
            An independent city investigation found the mayor engaged in "offensive and inappropriate behavior," but did not substantiate sexual harassment or retaliation.
      
    
            Doesn't sound like this is the hands-on approach to public service Minnesotans had in mind.

title: Democratic Senate Nominee in Alaska Used 'F****t' and R-Word, Multiple Staffers Claim
description:
Alaska Senate Nominee Mary Peltola
                          Ex Staffers Claim She Used R-Word, G
body:
Alaska Senate Nominee Mary Peltola
                          Ex Staffers Claim She Used R-Word, Gay Slurs
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 24, 2026
                            8:40 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Mary Peltola -- the Alaskan Democratic Senate nominee -- allegedly fired off numerous slurs and even shoved a staff member ... both while a sitting member of Congress and during her campaign.
      
    
            The New York Times released a report on Wednesday ... detailing the numerous unsavory incidents several former staff members alleged ... including four people who said Peltola used the gay slur "f****t" in their presence ... a claim her campaign strongly denied.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In a text message she sent about a commercial fisheries executive who posted a selfie with her, Peltola wrote, "F*** that r****d" ... a word her campaign says she recognizes now is inappropriate and regrets using.
      

            Back in 2024 -- during her tenure in Congress -- Peltola allegedly shoved a male staffer in the chest, causing him to stumble backwards. Peltola's team claims she didn't actually push him, instead insisting she ran into him accidentally.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Former staffers also told the NYT they watched her swipe papers off her desk in frustration ... looking like a scene out of the TV comedy, "Veep."
      
    
            In a statement to the Times, Peltola's staff blamed the loss of her mother and husband in 2023 as major stressors for her ... between that, raising her own grieving children and working in Congress, she struggled to deal with all of her emotions.
      
    
            Her spokesman Harry Child added, "Exaggerating and outright lying about moments from the hardest period of her life, and falsely presenting them as a pattern of behavior, is wrong."
      
    
            Other people the New York Times spoke to described more positive experiences with Peltola.

title: CNN and POLITCO Still Barred From White House Despite Judge's Ruling
description:
CNN and POLITICO
                          Hey Trump, We're Still Banned From The White House!!!
body:
CNN and POLITICO
                          Hey Trump, We're Still Banned From The White House!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 24, 2026
                            6:49 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 24, 2026
                                9:08 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
          Update
  
    
            9:07 AM PT -- CNN has been allowed back into the White House.
      
    
            President Trump apparently didn't get the memo ... CNN and POLITICO say their reporters are still being denied access to the White House despite a judge ordering the administration to restore access.
      
    
            As you know, the judge threw his support behind CNN, POLITICO and MS NOW by ruling Thursday that their journalists should immediately have their press credentials returned so they could enter the White House and cover the commander-in-chief.
      
    
            The ruling came in early Thursday, but when CNN and POLITICO reporters showed up to the White House to do their jobs, they reportedly were turned away.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The POLITICO reporter says his press credential was confiscated by the Secret Service.
      
    
            CNN reportedly sent Betsy Klein and a photojournalist ... but they were denied access and weren't given a reason.
      
    
            No word if MS NOW was also denied access.
      
    
            In his ruling, the judge stated, "The 'general rule' is that 'individuals must receive notice and an opportunity to be heard before the Government deprives them' of a constitutionally protected interest."
      
    
            You may recall ... the 3 news orgs sued Trump for trampling on their First Amendment rights after the president banned them several days ago for what he called fake reporting.
      
    
            We've reached out to the White House for comment ... so far, no word back.
